beginner.summary: For developers, operations engineers, testers and support staff who run or build services but have not yet worked with telemetry in a structured way. Covers why observability matters, the five signal types (metrics, logs, traces, profiles and events), metric types, golden signals with the RED and USE methods, structured logging and log shipping, distributed tracing and context propagation, automatic and manual instrumentation, querying metrics, logs and traces, label cardinality, dashboard and alert design, first SLIs, signal correlation, host and container telemetry, and a first-responder investigation routine. Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Jaeger and the OpenTelemetry SDKs appear as example tools; every idea is taught so it transfers to any commercial or open-source backend.
prerequisites: Has built, deployed or supported at least one web application or API and can read code in Python, Java, Go or JavaScript
Uses a terminal confidently, including curl, environment variables and reading command output
Has a laptop with Docker and Docker Compose installed, at least 8 GB of RAM and rights to pull container images
outcomes: Explain what metrics, logs, traces, profiles and events each answer, and choose the right signal for a given question
Instrument a web service with OpenTelemetry so it emits structured logs, RED metrics and traces that share a trace ID
Query metrics, logs and traces to locate a latency or error problem and build a service dashboard that shows it
Write symptom-based alerts and first SLIs, and follow a repeatable workflow from alert to likely cause

intermediate.summary: For engineers who already instrument services and use dashboards and alerts, and now need to run observability for a team or a Kubernetes platform. advanced.summary: For senior engineers, SRE leads, platform owners and architects who are responsible for observability across many teams and need to set its strategy, scale and budget. Covers maturity assessment and strategy, telemetry cost models, scaling metric, log and trace storage, pipeline resilience and loss accounting, wide events for high-cardinality analysis, eBPF-based zero-code telemetry, serverless and LLM application observability, multi-tenancy and access control, telemetry security and privacy, anomaly detection, hypothesis-driven investigation and topology-aware root cause, instrumentation testing in CI, vendor migration, on-call health, business telemetry and an enterprise platform capstone. Open-source tools are used for the labs; Datadog, Dynatrace, Splunk, New Relic and AppDynamics are discussed as examples when comparing build and buy options.
prerequisites: Has completed the intermediate level or has run a collector pipeline, SLOs and burn-rate alerts for production services
Has operated Kubernetes in production and can read Go, Python or Java code and Terraform or Helm configuration
Has access to a cloud account or a Kubernetes cluster with at least 8 CPU cores, 32 GB of RAM and S3-compatible object storage
outcomes: Assess observability maturity and write a funded multi-year strategy with cost models, ownership and success measures
Design scalable, resilient and multi-tenant telemetry storage and pipelines with measured data loss and controlled cost
Observe hard environments including eBPF-instrumented legacy services, serverless functions and LLM agents
Lead complex investigations with wide events, anomaly detection and topology, and run a vendor migration without blind spots
